Chapter Bylaws Article I. Preamble Sigma Omega Nu Latina Interest Sorority, Inc. was established at California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo by eight young women as a way to unite and involve its members in a bond of sisterhood through cultural, academic and social means. It is the intent of the organization to abide by the pertinent University regulations. Article II. Mission Statement Sigma Omega Nu is an organization that is built on academics, cultura, and sisterhood. Sigma Omega Nu provides a support system, cultura awareness, and a long-live sisterhood. It is a comfort zone where respect, accountability, and compassion are given and learned for womxn and the community. Article III. Vision Statement Sigma Omega Nu, Latina Interest Sorority, Inc. offers a unique sisterly experience for empowering womxn, by creating scholastic excellence, bringing cultura awareness, and providing a sisterhood bond in higher education. Article IV. Purpose The purpose of this Sorority shall be to strive for sisterhood, scholastic excellence, self- improvement, and Latina awareness and provide community service on the University Campus of very corresponding Chapter, as well as in the community. Article V. Identification Section A. Organization Identification The official name of this sorority is Sigma Omega Nu, Latina Interest Sorority, Inc. This name may be used interchangeably with Sigma Omega Nu, or the Greek letters ΣΩΝ. The name Sigma Omega Nu shall be used in the remainder of this document. The informal nicknames of “SON” and “Sunnies” may also be used to identify the Sorority, however these nicknames may only be used for informal identification purposes only. Section B. National Board: The collective term used to refer to the National Board Members 2. Chapters: The collective term used to refer to Sigma Omega Nu’s Undergraduate and Alumnae Chapters. 3. Active Members: Those members currently enrolled at a university where an Undergraduate Chapter of Sigma Omega Nu exists and who currently hold Active Status at their respective Chapter. See Article VI. Membership Section B. Active Status 4. Inactive Members: Those members currently enrolled at a university where an Undergraduate Chapter of Sigma Omega Nu exists and who currently hold Inactive Status at their respective Chapter. See Article VI. Membership Section C. Inactive Status. 5. Alumnae Members: The collective term used to refer to those members who have graduated from an accredited University. 6. Chapter Active Alumnae: Those Alumnae Members who hold Active Status at an Undergraduate Chapter. See Article VI. Membership Section D. Alumnae Status 7. National Active Alumnae: Those Alumnae Members who hold Active Status at the National Level, but not at any individual Chapter. See Article VI. Membership Section D. Alumnae Status. 8. General Members: Those members who do not otherwise meet the definition of Active, Inactive, or Alumnae Members. See Article VI. Membership Section E General Member Status 9. Sigma Omega Nu Members: The collective term used to refer to any and all members of Sigma Omega Nu, regardless of status or office held. 10. Good Standing: The term used to indicate that an individual Sister or an entire Chapter is fulfilling their duties and responsibilities, regardless of status. See Article VI. Membership for duties and responsibilities required of individual Sisters. 11. Probation: The disciplinary status assigned to an individual Sister or an entire Chapter as a result of failure to perform their duties and/or fulfill their responsibilities. 12. Suspension: The disciplinary status assigned to an individual Sister or an entire Chapter as a result of failure to perform their duties and/or fulfill their responsibilities. Suspension is a more severe status than Probation. See Article XVI. Suspension in these Chapter Bylaws and Article XVI. Chapters in the National Board Bylaws for additional information. 13. Deactivation: The process through which a Sister is no longer recognized as a member of Sigma Omega Nu. This may be voluntarily requested by the Sister, or may be imposed by the Sorority as a disciplinary sanction following a Judicial Review. 14. Simple Majority: During a meeting in which a quorum is present, a simple majority vote means 51% of those eligible to vote. 15. Plurality of Votes: In an election, the candidate that receives the most votes, even if not the majority. Article VI. Membership Section A. Requirements for Membership Membership is open to all those identifying as women who believe in and support the objectives of Sigma Omega Nu. Sigma Omega Nu does not discriminate against on the basis of race, religion, creed, sexual preferences, political affiliation, appearance or disabilities. All individuals interested in joining Sigma Omega Nu must undergo a period of Pledgeship. This organization or any of its members shall not conspire to commit any act, which causes or is likely to cause bodily danger or physical or emotional harm to any member of the campus community, surrounding communities, and/or any other member(s) of the Sorority. Minimum Grade Point Average. All potential members and initiated members of Sigma Omega Nu must maintain a minimum term grade point average of 2.3 and a minimum cumulative grade point average of 2.5 or higher AND must be in good academic standing with the University where the Chapter is established. 3. University Requirements. If the University at which the Chapter is established has additional or more stringent requirements for member of Greek life above and beyond those required by Sigma Omega Nut, those requirements must be abided by. This may include, but is not limited to: a higher minimum grade point average, having completed a set number of academic terms before pledgeship, etc. Section B. Active Status All members are considered fully Active from the date of their crossing, unless otherwise allowed. 1. Requirements a. All Active Members must maintain a minimum term grade point average of 2.3 and a minimum cumulative grade point average of 2.5 or higher and must be in Good Academic Standing with the University. b. Undergraduate members are required to be enrolled full-time and graduate students are required to be enrolled at least half-time at the University where the Chapter is established. c. If a member joins Sigma Omega Nu as an undergraduate, and pursues post-baccalaureate or graduate studies at a university where a Chapter is established, she is not required to be an Active member of the Chapter. However, they are encouraged to remain Active during the course of their studies. 2. Rights, Responsibilities and Duties a. Active Members are granted full rights without restriction to discuss and debate during General Meetings; vote; elect officers; hold an officer or chair position; and attend Sorority events and activities. b. Active Members are responsible for remaining in Good Standing by: i. Actively participating in all Chapter events and activities, including General Meetings, emergency meetings, Meetings of the Minds, elections, fundraising events, community service, philanthropy events, rush & recruitment events, pledgeship events & activities, and other events deemed mandatory by the Chapter, including events or activities required by Chapter Standards. ii. Actively participating in any other event or activity deemed mandatory by the Chapter, after having been designated as a mandatory event or activity with a simple majority vote. iii. Paying all dues and fines such that she has a clear account balance at the start of each quarter/semester. iv. Completing 30 hours of community service each year (10 hours per quarter or 15 hours per semester). Of the 30 hours, 10 hours must be dedicated to the specified Chapter philanthropy. v. Completing 6 library study hours per week, and document as required by the Vice President vi. Submitting all class schedules, transcripts, progress reports and any other academic information requested by the Vice President. vii. Faithfully executing the duties of any office or committee chair positions held. viii. Abiding by all Bylaws, Standing Rules, and Policies established by Sigma Omega Nu. -- 8 of 36 --

In the event a Sister is unable to attend a mandatory event or activity, she is responsible for submitting a Letter of Excuse to the Sergeant at Arms a minimum of twenty-four (24) hours prior to the event. The Letter will be read and voted on at the next General Meeting. A simple majority is required to approve the letter and excuse the absence. If the Letter is not approved, the Sister will be fined accordingly. See also Chapter Standing Rules, Article II. 3. Exceptions a. Graduating Seniors. Members who are in their final terms and are not enrolled in the required number of units identified above, are considered Active without restriction. To qualify for this exception, a member must submit a written Graduation Plan to the Chapter’s Vice President by the first week of the term in which they fall below the required units. The Vice President will maintain these Graduation Plans on file, and the Executive Board may request updates if a member’s graduation timeline changes. Failure to submit or update a Graduation Plan may result in a review of the member’s Active Status. The Graduation Plan must include: i. A list of all remaining courses required for their degree, ii. The academic term(s) in which they expect to complete those courses, iii. Their anticipated graduation date, and iv. An explanation of their enrollment status, including any circumstances outside their control (for example, courses offered only in specific terms, prerequisite sequencing, course conflicts, or departmental restrictions). b. Academic Probation with the Sorority. Members who have fallen below Sigma Omega Nu’s minimum required grade point average but are s still above the University’s minimum required Grade Point Average, are considered Active but with restrictions. These restrictions are: i. Must participate in the Chapter’s Mentorship Program, and abide by all requirements of the Program. ii. Ineligible to hold office or participate in committees. iii. Unable to participate in Pledgeship events or activities. iv. Ineligible to be selected as a Personal Big Sister. v. If the Sister’s GPA does not improve after two consecutive quarters/semesters, she will automatically be placed on Inactive Status for the following term. See Section C. Inactive Status below. c. Off-Campus Programs. A member is relieved from attendance obligations, but otherwise considered fully Active, while participating in any University-sanctioned off-campus programs. This includes study abroad programs and co-ops or internships that require the member to relocate away from the University for the duration of the program. All other responsibilities, including financial obligations, still apply. d. Personal Hardship. In the event a Sister faces personal hardship, such as financial difficulties or significant health conditions, she may be relieved of financial obligations for a period of time. She must present a letter to the Executive Board explaining her circumstances and identifying a set amount of time she is requesting to be excused from financial obligations. A ¾ majority of Executive Board is required to pass the request. 4. Honors & Recognition a. Gold Member. Inactive Status If a Sister is unable to meet the obligations of Active Status, they may be placed on Inactive Status. This status may be requested or, in certain cases, applied automatically. 1. Requesting Inactive Status a. A Sister may request Inactive Status for any reason. Normally, eligibility requires at least two consecutive semesters or three consecutive quarters of Active Status, not including the term in which they crossed. b. Exceptions: A Sister who has not yet fulfilled this minimum requirement may still request Inactive Status if personal, academic, health or financial circumstances significantly affect their ability to remain Active. c. Requests must be submitted in writing to the Chapter President within two weeks of the start of the academic term. Requests will be reviewed and voted on no later than the third General Meeting of the term. Approval requires a simple majority vote of the Chapter’s Active members present, provided quorum has been met. d. The Chapter President must notify the Sister in writing of the decision regarding their Inactive Status request prior to the next General Meeting. Notification must be delivered through email, and a copy of the decision shall be retained in the Chapter’s records. e. If a request is denied, the Sister may appeal the decision (please refer to Section E. Status Appeals). f. Inactive Status may not be granted for more than one semester/quarter per academic year. 2. Automatic Inactive Status a. A Sister on Academic Probation with the Sorority for more than two semesters/quarters will automatically be placed on Inactive Status. b. A Sister on Academic Probation with the University will automatically be placed on Inactive Status with the Chapter. c. The Chapter’s Vice President must notify the Sister in writing when Automatic Inactive Status is applied. 3. Rights, Responsibilities and Duties a. Suspension A Sister on Suspension Status is not considered in Good Standing with the Sorority for the full duration of the Suspension period. a. Any member may be placed in Suspension Status with privileges withdrawn for the following reasons: i. As a sanction resulting from a formal Judicial Review, for one of the offenses listed below ii. If the member is suspended from the University due to inappropriate actions by the member. iii. If a member is named in a sexual assault allegation or incident, they will be placed in Suspension Status for the duration of the Sexual Assault Judicial Review. See the Sexual Assault Judicial Review Procedures for additional information. b. Offenses. If a Judicial Review determines any of the following offenses did in fact occur, Suspension status is merited. i. Physical assault of any other individual ii. Sexual assault or harassment of any other individual iii. Repeated refusal to pay dues owed and/or fines incurred c. Restrictions i. The member will automatically be removed from any officer or committee position(s) held ii. The member is prohibited from participating in any Chapter, Colony, and National events or activities iii. The member is prohibited from using or wearing any insignia or paraphernalia of Sigma Omega Nu or its Chapters. d. Duration i. If a member is suspended as the result of a Judicial Review, the duration of the suspension period shall be unanimously agreed upon by the Judicial Review Committee. Two weeks prior to the end of her suspension period, the member must contact the Executive Board to discuss her suspension. If the member has followed the restrictions of her suspension, she may regain full privileges. ii. If a member is suspended in conjunction with suspension by the University, the duration of the suspension period shall be the same as that identified by the University. If the University removes the suspension status, the member may regain full privileges. iii. If the duration of the suspension lasts for more than one term, the member will return to whichever status she held prior to being placed on suspension. She will be held to all rights, responsibilities, duties, and restrictions of that status for the remainder of the term. Section E. Status Appeals 1. Appealing Denial of Inactive Status Request a. Transfers A Sister may transfer her Active Status to another Chapter under two conditions: 1. The Sister transfers to another University where another Chapter of Sigma Omega Nu exists. 2. The Sister transfers to another University that is within the local commuting area of another University where a Chapter of Sigma Omega Nu exists. The following process must be followed in order for a Sister to transfer her Active Status to another Chapter. 1. The Sister must pay all outstanding dues and fines owed to her initiating Chapter, return any Chapter property, and complete any required transition meetings. 2. The Sister must submit a letter to the Executive Board of her initiating Chapter notifying them of the transfer to another University, including her date of transfer, and the intent to transfer to another Chapter. This letter must be submitted no later than the second to last meeting of the quarter or semester prior to the transfer. No vote is required for this letter. 3. The Sister must submit a letter to the Executive Board of the Chapter at the University she will be transferring to notifying them of the transfer to their university, including the date of transfer, and requesting Active Status with the Chapter. This letter must be submitted no later than the second to last meeting of the quarter or semester prior to the transfer. No vote is required for this letter, but the Executive Board of the transfer Chapter is required to notify its Chapter Membership of the transfer. 4. The Executive Board of the initiating Chapter will submit a letter to the Executive Board of the transfer Chapter notifying the transfer Chapter that the Sister has completed all requirements in order to transfer. Once this letter is received, the Executive Board of the transfer Chapter will add the member to any Chapter distribution lists, group chats, etc. and notify the member of the date, time, and location of the next General Meeting. 5. Once the member has been accepted as an Active member of the transfer Chapter, the Executive Board of the transfer Chapter must submit a letter to the Executive Board of the initiating Chapter stating that the transfer has been complete. 6. The Sister who has transferred to another University and Chapter must continue to provide updated contact and degree information to her initiating Chapter. It is the responsibility of the member transferring and the Executive Board of both Chapters to complete this process and keep all records accordingly. Any Sister who transfers to another Chapter will still remain on the Chapter member roster of her initiating Chapter and retain her crossing information from that Chapter. She will not be added to the scroll of the transfer Chapter, but must be added to the Chapter Active Roster submitted to National Board. Section G. Alumnae Status -- 13 of 36 --

Alumnae Status -- 13 of 36 -- Approved 03/22/2026; Effective 07/01/2026 15 1. Requirements a. In order to be considered an Alumna of Sigma Omega Nu, one must have completed all undergraduate and/or graduate courses and have received a diploma from an accredited four- year University. 2. Rights, Responsibilities, and Duties a. Alumnae are responsible for remaining in Good Standing by: i. Maintaining a clear balance with any Chapter(s) previously affiliated with ii. Providing updated contact, graduation, and degree information with her initiating Chapter. iii. Paying for her participating in all Sigma Omega Nu activities, when required. 3. Restrictions a. If an Alumna Member intends to participate in any Chapter event, including General Meetings, she must notify the Chapter President of her intent to participate at least 24 hours in advance of the event. b. Alumnae Members may attend General Meetings, but are not allowed to participate in discussion, debate, or voting. 4. Chapter Active Alumnae a. Alumnae who desire to maintain Active Status at an Undergraduate Chapter are required to submit a letter requesting Active Status within the first two weeks of each term. A simple majority vote of the Active Membership is needed for letter to pass. If the request is denied, there is no appeal process. b. Active Alumnae must abide by all of the requirements and expectations of an Active Member as identified in Section B. Active Status above, except for the enrollment requirements. Additionally, Active Alumnae must abide by any requirements and restrictions imposed by the University with regards to Active Alumnae. c. Chapter Active Alumnae dues will be determined by the Chapter, in accordance with Article XII. Finances, Section A. Dues. Half of this amount shall go towards the Academic Honor Society Scholarship. 5. National Active Alumnae a. Alumnae who desire to maintain Active Status with the Organization but not at an Undergraduate Chapter may request National Active Status from the National Board. b. National Active Alumnae status does not also grant the member Chapter Active Alumnae status. If the member wishes to also hold Chapter Active Alumnae Status, she must request that through the individual Chapter, as outlined above. c. National Active Alumnae dues are determined by the National Board. 25% of National Alumnae Dues shall go towards the Annual National Board Scholarship Fund, with the remainder going towards the National general fund. d. Dues for National Active Alumnae are to be paid directly to the National Vice President of Finance. See the National Board Bylaws for National Active Alumnae dues amounts. Section H. General Members may attend General Meetings, but are not allowed to participate in discussion, debate, or vote. Section I. New Members 1. After becoming a New Member, the New Class must remove the cover sheet from their binder, and replace it with one that has the Greek Letters ΣΩΝ somewhere on it. 2. Before the next general meeting, the Pledge Mothers will hold the Post Pledgeship Workshop with the New Members to review the Chapter Bylaws and Chapter Standing Rules, as well as explain how a general meeting is held. See also Standardized Chapter Pledgeship, Article XX. New Members. 3. At the first General Meeting after crossover, each officer will conduct her business as usual. At the conclusion of her announcements, the officer will ask the New Members if they have any questions. At the end of the meeting, the President shall ask the New Members if they have any more questions about the officers, their duties, or the general running of a meeting. 4. Should there be any vacant positions at the time, the New Members shall be nominated for any positions they are eligible to hold, and given a week to review the position description before elections. Section J. Multiple Memberships Members of Sigma Omega Nu may join other Greek lettered organizations as long as membership in those organizations meet the following requirements: 1. Honorary Membership: Honorary club or fraternity where membership or entitlement is given in recognition of the sister’s excellence in their course of study or contributions to the University. Membership is by invitation only. 2. Professional Membership: Any member of this Sorority may join a professional, service or leadership-based co-ed fraternity. These organizations are founded on career development, community service or leadership development. They do not prohibit members of social fraternities or sororities from membership. 3. Restrictions: No member of this Sorority may be a member of any other social sorority or fraternity. Any member wishing to join one of these organizations must first complete Sigma Omega Nu’s deactivation process prior to seeking membership. Those interested in joining Sigma Omega Nu must provide proof of having completed the deactivation process of any previous organization(s) prior to beginning the Sigma Omega Nu membership process. Article VII. Officers Section A. Officers Sigma Omega Nu shall consist of the following eighteen officers: President, Vice President, Sergeant-At- Arms, Treasurer, Vice President of Communications, Auditor, Risk Management Officer, Commissioner of -- 15 of 36 --

sorority or fraternity. Any member wishing to join one of these organizations must first complete Sigma Omega Nu’s deactivation process prior to seeking membership. Chapter Standards Mission Statement “Sigma Omega Nu’s foundation was built on academics, cultura, and sisterhood. Some objectives are to strengthen cultural, personal and educational goals while promoting moral, academic and family support. Through mutual support and encouragement, Sigma Omega Nu instills the importance of education and academic success in the college environment.” All members of Sigma Omega Nu strive to uphold the principles of the Sorority’s Mission Statement. It is also a requirement of each Chapter to promote and encourage these principles. The Chapter Standards program was created to help guide the Chapters towards positive and continued development and improvement. Annual Submittal & Review: Chapter Standards shall be submitted annually and are due no later than June 30th. Each submission must document Chapter activity from July 1st of the previous year through June 30th of the current year. All Chapter Standards documents must be uploaded to the designated National Google Drive Folder by the June 30th deadline. Only Chapters that submit their Chapter Standards by June 30th will be eligible for Chapter of the Year recognition. Any Chapter that fails to submit its Chapter Standards by June 30th will be considered late and subject to the following consequences: • Submissions received between July 1st and July 15th Chapters that submit their Chapter Standards binder between July 1st and July 15th will be placed on Probation for the following academic term, regardless of the final score or rating earned. • Submissions not received by July 15th Chapters that fail to submit their Chapter Standards binder by July 15th will be placed on Suspension for the following academic term. Suspension imposed due to failure to submit by this deadline will not be eligible to be lifted, regardless of points earned upon eventual submission. Submissions must consist only of the required forms and spreadsheets specified in the Chapter Standards credit requirements. All documents must be converted to PDF format and clearly labeled with the corresponding Section and Number. Materials submitted in an incorrect format, improperly labeled, or not explicitly required will not be reviewed and will not receive credit. The National Board will review each Chapter’s submission collectively, and assign a final score and rating in accordance with the established scoring system. Final scores, written feedback, and the Chapter’s official status will be issued via email to all Chapters no later than August 30th. Feedback will identify areas for -- 1 of 17 -- Approved 03/22/2026; Effective 07/01/2026 2 improvement for the upcoming academic year. Chapters receiving a rating of Probation or Suspension will be issued a formal Improvement Plan outlining required corrective actions for the following academic term. Chapters that fail to meet the requirements of their Improvement Plan will be placed on Suspension (if previously on Probation) or will remain on Suspension for the remainder of the academic year. Points & Ratings The Chapter Standards are organized based on a point system. Points are given for the successful completion of a credit. The point system breakdown is as follows: Obligatory: 50 points The Obligatory credits are required to be completed by every Chapter each year in order to be recognized as a Chapter of Sigma Omega Nu. Most of the Obligatory credits are for the Chapter’s commitments to the National Board. Any Chapter that does not complete all Obligatory requirements is automatically placed on Suspension, regardless of overall points earned. Required: 20 points In addition to the Obligatory credits, the Required credits are considered the basic foundation for the successful running of a Chapter. Expected: 10 points Expected credits are required activities that support the continued growth, development, and sustainability of the Chapter. Article IX, Section F of the Chapter Bylaws. A basic outline of Robert’s Rules of Order is below. 1. Agenda a. All meetings shall follow a fixed agenda as listed in Section A above. b. If anyone wants to discuss anything not already on the agenda, they must request it be added to the agenda before it is approved. 2. Motions [a proposal to take a stand on an issue] a. The proposal cannot contradict the National Bylaws, Chapter Bylaws, Standing Rules or University regulations -- 3 of 12 -- Approved 03/22/2026; Effective 07/01/2026 4 b. The motion must be specific to the issue that it deals with. c. The motion must be in the form: “I motion to ........... ” 3. Second to the Motion a. A second to the motion is needed by another member b. If there is no second the motion dies c. There is no discussion until there is a second to the motion 4. Discussion a. Discussion is open to all Active Members. b. Discussion from Inactive Members or Alumni may only be voiced if Active Membership agrees c. The member who made the original motion shall explain her motion, show evidence to support, explain why this would work best, etc. d. Other members may ask questions or comment about the motion e. Other members may suggest amendments to the current motion. f. The Sergeant at Arms shall limit the amount of time spent on discussion and can end it when she sees fit. 5. Re-state Motion a. Once discussion is closed by the Sergeant at Arms, the original motioner must restate the motion. b. The original motioner shall decide whether or not to incorporate suggested amendments made during the discussion. If so, the re-state motion must include those amendments. 6. Vote a. Once the motion has been re-stated, all eligible voting members shall vote on the motion. b. A simple majority (51%) affirmative vote is needed to pass the motion c. If the motion deals with money, a three-fourths (75%) affirmative vote is needed 7. Other Important Information a. A new motion cannot be made until the original motion dies or is voted on. b. Motions can be TABLED, meaning that the motion can be set to be discussed at another time (such as the next meeting) c. c. All motions, including who motioned, who seconded, any amendments, and the final vote, shall be documented in the meeting minutes. Sexual Assault Protocol This protocol has been established to provide an appropriate and coordinated response to survivors of sexual assault. Definitions (taken from the Clery Act): • Sexual Assault: Any sexual act directed against another person, without consent of the victim, including instance where the victim is incapable of giving consent. • Rape: Penetration, no matter how slight, of the vagina or anus, with any body part of object, or oral penetration by a sex organ of another person, without the consent of the victim. This offense includes the rape of both males and females [all genders]. • Fondling: Touching of the private body parts of another person for the purpose of sexual gratification, without the consent of the victim, including instances where the victim is incapable of giving consent because of his/her age or because of his/her temporary or permanent mental capacity. • Statutory Rape: Sexual intercourse with a person who is under the age of consent (18 years old). Disclosure: Any time you are informed by a member that they have been a victim of sexual abuse or sexual assault you should do the following: • Listen respectfully and let the survivor know that you care. Let them know that you are there for them and receptive to what they are sharing. • Thank the survivor for telling you. Allow survivors to disclose as little or as much about the assault as they are comfortable sharing. • Validate their feelings about the experience. Let them know that you believe them and that what they went through is understandably painful. • Express to the survivor that you are sorry that s/he experienced such an event. • Avoid asking for specifics/details, defining the experience for the survivor, or exhibiting distraction. • Do not question the validity of the survivor’s claim. • Do not make excuses for the perpetrator. The perpetrator’s actions are inexcusable. • Allow survivors to direct their own recovery and to have control over their thoughts, feelings, and actions because a critical part of healing is regaining some sense of control of their lives. • Take care of yourself. Secondary trauma is real, and you should (while respecting the survivors’ confidentiality) turn to your own support system and be realistic about how much you can provide. A survivor may demand more of you than you are able to give. You may not be trained to manage a survivor’s recovery and may be emotionally exhausted. Be kind and honest with the survivor about what you are able to do, and encourage him or her to seek professional help through a hotline or therapist. -- 7 of 22 --

Reporting Options (External): An individual who has experienced an incident of sexual assault, sexual harassment, or sexual misconduct may report the incident at any time, regardless of how much time has elapsed since the incident occurred. Sigma Omega Nu is committed to supporting the rights of a person reporting an incident to make an informed choice among options and services available. • Reporting to Law Enforcement: An incident can be reported to law enforcement at any time, 24 hours a day/7 days a week, by calling 911. Offer to assist or accompany the survivor to do so, or offer to arrange for an advocate (if available) to accompany the survivor to make a report to law enforcement. Making a report to law enforcement does not commit the survivor to having the alleged assailant notified of the report, having an investigation conducted, or to pressing charges. Those decisions can be made at a later point. • Reporting to Title IX: A report can be made to your University’s Title IX office. The report will initiate a Title IX investigation by the University to determine if there has been a violation by a University community member of the University’s sexual misconduct policy. Chapter Judicial Review & Procedures This procedure must be followed during any judicial review that is requested by a Chapter for an individual Sister, regardless of their status (i.e., Active, Inactive, Alumna, etc.). The Code of Ethics and Officers’ Code of Ethics are intended to provide an ethical and moral base for this Sorority. Failure to uphold either shall result in appropriate and relevant consequences to be determined by the Judicial Review Committee. The following process shall be followed: 1. Confidentiality a. All matters related to the Judicial Review process must remain strictly confidential. b. Only members of the Judicial Review Committee may discuss the details of the case. c. The nature of the breach(es) and any sanctions imposed may not be shared outside of the Chapter, with the exception of the National Board. d. If guidance or support is needed, Chapters may contact the National Vice President of Parliamentary Procedures. 2. Initiating a Review a. At least one-third of the Active Membership must sign the written request describing the alleged breach(es). b. The request must then be submitted to the Chapter’s Sergeant at Arms and shall be presented at the Chapter’s next general meeting. i. chunks.content: Approved 07/26/2025 1 Sigma Omega Nu Latina Interest Sorority, Inc. National Board Alumnae Advisory Committee Article I. Name This organization shall be named Sigma Omega Nu National Board Alumnae Advisory Committee (SON, NBAAC). Article II. Purpose and Objectives The purpose of the committee is to advise the National Board on specific issues, when requested. The committee shall also hear appeals on decisions made by the National Board, including but not limited to deactivations and other Judicial Review sanctions. Article III. Membership Section 1. Requirements Membership on the committee shall consist of up to seven (7) alumnae members. At least four of the seven alumnae members must have completed at least one full term on the National Board and have been an alumna for at least five years. Active alumnae and chapter advisors are not eligible to serve on the committee. Ideally, membership should include alumnae from different chapters and graduation years, and diverse fields. The committee advises the National Board members and therefore, the committee members shall have no voting rights, except in cases of appeals. Members are expected to be professional, be available for virtual meetings, as needed, and not be swayed by personal relationships or ties to a specific chapter. Section 2. Admissions Process Interested alumnae shall submit a professional resume and letter of intent to the National Board via email at national.sunnies@gmail.com. The National Board shall appoint members who meet the membership requirements and these appointments shall be approved by the National Council. Interviews may be conducted, when necessary, but are not required. Section 3. Term Members shall serve no more than two successive terms, unless there are no other members requesting to join, in which case that member’s term may be extended with the approval of the National Board. Members may be reappointed following a one term hiatus. Terms shall begin on February 1st and end on January 31st. Section 4. Resignation Due to the voluntary nature of committee membership, members may resign at any point. As courtesy, a letter shall be submitted to the Alumnae Advisory Committee membership and the National Board President as soon as reasonably possible. -- 1 of 2 -- Approved 07/26/2025 2 If there is an appeal in process, members are expected to complete the appeal process before resigning. If members fail to do so, they will not be permitted to apply again for at least two years. Section 5. Responsibilities The responsibilities of Alumnae Advisory Committee members are to provide guidelines and recommendations of best sorority policies and practices (including short term and long term strategic goals). Alumnae Advisory Committee member recommendations shall be presented to the National Board in written form. The National Board will review recommendations and approve or deny implementation. Matters of discussion shall include, but are not limited to the following topics: • Disaffiliation cases • Branding of the sorority • Legal matters • Risk management practices • New member initiation • Financial matters • Other functions as needed The discussion including any documentation shared with the members of the committee shall be held as confidential and shall not be shared with any member, person or entity outside of the Alumnae Advisory Committee or the National Board. Article IV. Officers Members of the committee shall all be equal in standing and roles. The committee shall rotate the lead position for each meeting; unless one member is elected by the committee to lead for the term. Article V. Meetings Meetings shall be called as needed by the National Board President with at least 2 days written notice. Email or Text is acceptable as written notice. These meetings shall be held via teleconference. The minutes shall be taken by the designated Advisory Committee member and shall be kept for the term of the current membership. Alumnae Advisory Committee members are permitted to attend all National Board and National Council meetings. Article VI. Amendments Amendments to the Committee Bylaws may be recommended by any member of the Alumnae Advisory Committee and/or the National Board and shall follow the proposal process. Article VII. Adoption Adoption of the Bylaws and Procedures of this Committee shall be made effective immediately following approval of the Sigma Omega Nu National Board.

National Bylaws Article I. Preamble Sigma Omega Nu Latina Interest Sorority, Inc. established its National Board as a way of uniting all of its Chapters under one official board. This organization shall be a non-profit public benefit organization. Article II. Mission Statement Sigma Omega Nu is an organization that is built on academics, cultura, and sisterhood. Sigma Omega Nu provides a support system, cultura awareness, and a long-live sisterhood. It is a comfort zone where respect, accountability, and compassion are given and learned for womxn and the community. Article III. Vision Statement Sigma Omega Nu, Latina Interest Sorority, Inc. offers a unique sisterly experience for empowering womxn, by creating scholastic excellence, bringing cultura awareness, and providing a sisterhood bond in higher education. Article IV. Purpose The purpose of the National Board shall be to act as the guiding board for Sigma Omega Nu Latina Interest Sorority, Inc. The National Board shall provide leadership and guidance for all Sigma Omega Nu members and Chapters to successfully strive for scholastic excellence, Latina/o cultural awareness, sisterhood, community service, self-improvement and professional development. The National Board shall provide general guidance to members and Chapters for their continual progress and advancement. The National Board may act as a mediator between Chapters in order to provide solutions for conflicts or disputes. The National Board shall also be responsible for overseeing all aspects of the Expansion Process. Article V. Identification Section A. Organization Identification The official name of this sorority is Sigma Omega Nu, Latina Interest Sorority, Inc. This name may be used interchangeably with Sigma Omega Nu or the Greek ΣΩΝ. The name Sigma Omega Nu shall be used in the remainder of this document. The informal nicknames of “SON” and “Sunnies” may also be used to identify the Sorority however these nicknames may only be used for informal identification purposes only. Section B. National Board Members: Those members currently holding National Office as identified in Article V. below. This includes the Executive Cabinet, the National Directors, and the Members at Large. 3. National Board: The collective term used to refer to the National Board Officers and National Board -- 6 of 28 --

Sigma Omega Nu Members: The collective term used to refer to any and all members of Sigma Omega Nu, regardless of status or office held. 12. Good Standing: The term used to indicate that an individual Sister or an entire Chapter is fulfilling their duties and responsibilities, regardless of status. See Article VI. Membership for duties and responsibilities required of individual Sisters 13. Probation: The disciplinary status assigned to an individual Sister or an entire Chapter as a result of failure to perform their duties and/or fulfill their responsibilities. 14. Suspension: The disciplinary status assigned to an individual Sister or an entire Chapter as a result of failure to perform their duties and/or fulfill their responsibilities. Suspension is a more severe status than Probation. See Article XVI. Suspension in these Chapter Bylaws and Article XVI. Chapters in the National Board Bylaws for additional information. 15. Deactivation: The process through which a Sister is no longer recognized as a member of Sigma Omega Nu. This may be voluntarily requested by the Sister, or may be imposed by the Sorority as a disciplinary sanction following a Judicial Review. 16. Simple Majority: During a meeting in which a quorum is present, a simple majority vote means 51% of those eligible to vote. 17. Plurality of Votes: In an election, the candidate that receives the most votes, even if not the majority. Article VI. Membership National Board membership is open to all Sigma Omega Nu Active Members and Alumnae Members, so long as they meet the qualifications for the individual officer position. There will be no discrimination on the basis of initiating chapter, cultural identify, religion, creed, sexual preference, political affiliation, assigned sex, or disabilities. Section A. All Directors must have a minimum of one year’s membership as a Sister of Sigma Omega Nu. 4. Members at Large must meet the eligibility requirements identified in Article VII. Multiple Memberships Members of Sigma Omega Nu may join other Greek lettered organizations, so long as their membership meets the following requirements: 1. Honorary Membership Any member of this Sorority may join an honorary club or fraternity, or hold an honorary title. Membership or entitlement is given in recognition of the Sister’s excellence in their course of study or contributions to the University. Membership is by invitation only. 2. Professional Membership Any member of this Sorority may join a professional, service or leadership based co-ed fraternity. These organizations are founded on career development, community service or leadership development. They do not prohibit members of social fraternities or sororities from membership. 3. Prohibition No member of this Sorority may be a member of any other socially or culturally based sorority or fraternity. Any member wishing to join one of these organizations must first complete Sigma Omega Nu’s deactivation process prior to seeking membership. Any woman interested in joining Sigma Omega Nu must provide proof of having completed the deactivation of any previous organization(s) prior to beginning the Sigma Omega Nu membership process. Robert’s Rules of Order Meetings shall follow Robert’s Rules of Order, as specified in Article XIII, Section H of the National Bylaws. A basic outline of Robert’s Rules of Order is below. 1. Agenda a. All meetings shall follow a fixed agenda as listed in Section A above. b. If anyone wants to discuss anything not already on the agenda, they must request it be added to the agenda before it is approved. 2. Motions a. Obtain the Floor Those permitted to participate in discussion must raise their hand in order to be recognized by the National Vice President of Parliament. -- 5 of 15 -- Approved 08/08/2026 b. Make a Motion With the expectation of proposals seeking to modify governing documents, a motion cannot contradict any existing governing document. c. The motion must be clear and specific to the topic being discussed. It must be stated in the form of “I motion to…” or “I move to…”Second to the Motion One other member permitted to participate in discussion must second the motion. There will be no further discussion on the motion until there is a second to the motion. If there is no second to the motion, the motion dies and there is no further discussion. If the motion dies, a new motion can be made. d. Discuss and Debate the Motion The original motioner may explain the motion, show evidence to support, explain why this would work best, etc. Those permitted to participate in discussion are allowed to ask questions and voice their opinions. Friendly amendments may be proposed by others, but need not be accepted by the original motioner. e. The National Vice President of Parliament shall limit the amount of time spent on discussion and can end it when she sees fit. Re-state the Motion Once discussion is concluded, the original motioner must restate the motion. If the original motioner decides to include any proposed amendments suggested during discussion, the motion must be restated incorporating those amendments. Discussion on the amended motion may continue if necessary. f. Vote on the Motion If there is no further discussion, the vote is taken. Only those eligible to vote are permitted to do so. A simple majority (51%) affirmative vote is needed to pass the motion. For matters concerning finances or revisions to the governing documents, a three-fourths (75%) affirmative vote is needed for a motion to pass. g. New Motions A new motion cannot be presented unless the existing motion dies, is voted on, or is tabled h. Tabling a Motion A motion may be tabled for a set period of time or indefinitely, to be discussed at a later time. All motions, including who motioned, who seconded, any amendments, and the final vote, shall be documented in the meeting minutes. Additionally, the National Vice President of Parliament shall keep a separate log of all motions passed and the date they take effect.

P U R P O S E The Director of Expansion oversees all expansion efforts that could potentially result in the establishment of new Undergraduate Chapters of Sigma Omega Nu. The Director of Expansion is responsible for presentations to interest groups, Greek Councils, and potential Chapter Advisors. She monitors the progress of all interest groups and Official Interest Groups. Once a new Chapter is established, she is responsible for mentoring the new chapter in their first few months of establishment, and transitioning the new Chapter to oversight by the NVP of Undergraduate Affairs and the applicable Regional Director. P A R T I I . E X P A N S I O N O V E R V I E W The expansion process consists of four phases: Interest Group; Official Interest Group; Colony; Chapter. Each phase is described below. S e c t i o n A . P h a s e O n e : I n t e r e s t G r o u p The Interest Group process is led by the group of interested women themselves. Typically, though not always, the group of women has already explored the other sororities established at their campus and determined they were not the right fit for them. They may have learned about Sigma Omega Nu through other Greek organizations, through an internet search, or by having met Sisters of Sigma Omega Nu. At this point, they have no obligation to this Sorority. They may also be communicating with the national director of expansion from one or more other sororities, to figure out which organization fits them best. If the interested women determine they want to move forward with establishing a Chapter of Sigma Omega Nu, they must meet certain minimum requirements before they can move on to the next Phase. S e c t i o n B . P h a s e T w o : O f f i c i a l I n t e r e s t G r o u p This phase is overseen by the Director of Expansion, and may only be started once all of the minimum interest group requirements have been met by all interested members. Once recognized as an Official Interest Group, the members and the group itself are officially and legally associated with the Sorority. During this phase, the Official Interest Group will work on establishing many of the business requirements of a Chapter, such as establishing a bank account, selecting an advisor, and beginning the process of Council recognition. S e c t i o n C . P h a s e T h r e e : C o l o n y Once the Official Interest Group completes the requirements of that phase, and the National Board agrees to continue with the expansion process, the Official Interest Group will become a Colony. The Colony phase is equivalent to Pledgeship at an established Chapter, and is led by Colony Directors that are elected for each specific Colony. Through this process, the women will learn about the inner workings of the Sorority, and what it means to be a Sister and Founding Sister of Sigma Omega Nu. S e c t i o n D . I N T E R E S T G R O U P The following process should be followed during the Interest Group phase. S e c t i o n A . C o n t a c t f r o m I n t e r e s t e d W o m e n Interested women will contact Sigma Omega Nu through expansion@sigmaomeganu.org or through national.sunnies@gmail.com. The Director of Expansion should respond to the email as soon after receiving it as possible. Attach the Sigma Omega Nu Informational Brochure (PDF) to the email. S e c t i o n B . I n q u i r e w i t h t h e G r e e k C o u n c i l Contact the appropriate Greek Council at the University. The Council President and/or Council Advisor should have contact information easily accessible on the University’s Greek Life website. If not, request this information from the interested women. The purpose of this initial contact is to find out if the University and/or the Greek Council are open for expansion considerations, and if so, what the Council’s expansion policies are. Include the Sigma Omega Nu Council Info Flyer (PDF) as an attachment to the email. The University’s Greek Life website will also usually indicate which Latina and/or multicultural sororities are already established on campus. This information, along with University demographics, will help the Director of Expansion gauge the likelihood of success of the potential future chapter. The Director of Expansion will need to be prepared with this information during the National Board’s discussion on whether or not to pursue establishing a chapter. If the University and/or the Council are not open for the addition of new organizations, ask if there is a known date for when they will be open again. There is a good chance they will not have a specific date in mind, and may be willing to accept a letter of interest to keep on file for when they are open for expansion. This information will need to be communicated back to the interested women. They will need to decide if they want to continue to pursue establishing a new chapter of Sigma Omega Nu on an unknown timeline, or if they want to re-consider joining an existing sorority. If the University and/or the Council are not open for expansion, the expansion process will effectively end at this step until such time as the University and Council are willing to consider new organizations, and the Interest Group is still willing to pursue the establishment of a new chapter. T y p e s o f G r e e k C o u n c i l s There are up to four councils that you will most likely interact with on any given campus. The first three councils listed here are almost always present, though in some cases only the first two. Each council is typically associated with an umbrella organization, but not always. 1. Panhellenic Council. The Panhellenic Council is the council for 26 traditional social sororities and fraternities for women. Many of these organizations were founded in the late 1800s and early 1900s, which is why some use the term “women’s fraternity” in their name. The National Panhellenic Conference (NPC) is the umbrella organization for these organizations. Occasionally, sororities that are not members of NPC may be included in the Panhellenic Council as associate members. This may happen when there are too few organizations to create and sustain multiple councils, or if the associate member organization wants access to the formal Panhellenic Council bid process. Religious-based sororities are most often associate members of the Panhellenic Council, but not always. 2. Inter-Fraternity Council. Often called IFC for short, this council represents the 75 traditional social fraternities for men. In recent years culturally based fraternities have become members of

Occasionally, sororities that are not members of NPC may be included in the Panhellenic Council as associate members. This may happen when there are too few organizations to create and sustain multiple councils, or if the associate member organization wants access to the formal Panhellenic Council bid process. Religious-based sororities are most often associate members of the Panhellenic Council, but not always. 2. Inter-Fraternity Council. Often called IFC for short, this council represents the 75 traditional social fraternities for men. In recent years culturally based fraternities have become members of -- 13 of 16 -- Dated 2021 14 the umbrella organization, North American Interfraternity Council (NIC) specifically for access to the larger pool of potential candidates. Religious-based fraternities are most often associate members of the Panhellenic Council, but not always. 3. Multicultural Council. The council created for culturally-based organizations typically has one of three names: Multicultural Greek Council (MGC), Cultural Greek Council (CGC), or United Sorority and Fraternity Council (USFC). There is usually no umbrella organization associated with this council, however there is an actual National Multicultural Greek Council that serves as an umbrella organization for 11 multicultural fraternities and sororities. The multicultural council will often include all fraternities and sororities that have some sort of cultural, religious, or gender focus, though occasionally these organizations may seek membership to the NPC or IFC councils for access to a larger pool of prospective new members. 4. National Pan-Hellenic Council. The NPHC, or Divine Nine, are the 9 original Black fraternities and sororities founded in the early 1900s. When there are not enough organizations on campus to sustain a dedicated NPHC, they will often be a member organization of the Multicultural Council. There are other councils that are less common, but are included here for your general awareness. 1. National Association of Latino Fraternal Organizations (NALFO). Umbrella organization for Latinx fraternities and sororities. There are very few established NALFO councils. 2. National APIDA Panhellenic Association (NAPA). Umbrella organization for Asian fraternities and sororities. 3. National Multicultural Greek Council (NMGC). Umbrella organization for recognized multicultural fraternities and sororities. Since Sigma Omega Nu is a member of NALFO, membership into a NALFO council is guaranteed. However, since so few NALFO councils exist, any future chapter would most likely be a member of the multicultural council. If uncertain which council a new chapter would belong to, reach out to the university’s Greek advisor. S e c t i o n B . Sorority History In September of 1996, eight young Latina women at California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo, gathered together to create a sorority that would fulfill an unmet need on campus. These eight women were Lina Medina, Landi Hueramo, Yesenia Hueramo, Sarai Sequeira, Nadia Quinonez, Cristina De Sanchez, Nancy Ruiz, and Zulema Gonzalez. The Latina interest sorority was born directly out of a Little Sister Program. Sigma Omega Nu is the first Latina interest sorority ever created at Cal Poly, San Luis Obispo. The purpose of this sorority is to create sisterhood, scholastic excellence, self-improvement, Latina/o awareness, and to provide community service. The women of Sigma Omega Nu feel this organization can help bring Latina women closer together while making Cal Poly life easier and more exciting. Sigma Omega Nu strives to provide its members with moral, academic, and family support. They also provide a sisterly atmosphere by strengthening cultural bonds, helping the community, and making an impact on all the young women out there. The formation of the sorority was completed when Cal Poly State University, San Luis Obispo, recognized Sigma Omega Nu as an organization on November 6, 1996. As sisters we strive to stand by one another through the good times as well as the bad. Sigma Omega Nu sisters will prosper and succeed in life. Article II. Symbols, Meanings and Facts Section A.
